spec_match.rationale: column-rule/row-rule in grid gaps, the before/after comparison with the border-hack, and the commented repeat() alternation accurately reflect css-gaps-1's shipped surface.

interactive.rationale: Four toggles (column, row, dashed, 4px) drive inline rule styles on the live editorial grid (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises an editorial card grid with separator rules and no extra elements — delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: Style/width/none permutations are covered, but support detection is only a static note — in this browser all four toggles appear inert with no live unsupported state — and repeat() alternation exists only as a comment.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5157805733183488 and the Chrome Developers gap-decorations blog.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the real surface and honestly fails 6 of 8 in this browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): page renders, grid shows no rules (expected here), and the screenshot exposes the two inactive toggles rendering as blank boxes; toggles were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

design_system.rationale: Invariant 6 regression: .toggle-btn sets background: var(--bg-ivory) without overriding color, so the global button color (--bg-ivory) renders 'dashed style' and 'thicker (4px)' as invisible light-on-light labels — visible as two blank buttons in the screenshot (bug history 308580a repeated); update() also hard-codes #ccc for the row rule instead of a variable.

accessibility.rationale: Toggles are native buttons but two are visually blank (contrast failure), none expose aria-pressed, and rule changes have no non-visual equivalent (acceptable for decorative lines, but the toggle state itself should be perceivable).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The grid steps down 3→2→1 columns at 600/400px and snippets scroll; clean at 1280px headless, ≈360px untested.

openQuestions.title: Fix the invisible toggle buttons (invariant 6: override color with background)
openQuestions.detail: .toggle-btn { background: var(--bg-ivory); } inherits color: var(--bg-ivory) from the global button rule in public/styles.css, so the non-active 'dashed style' and 'thicker (4px)' buttons render blank (screenshot evidence, same failure class as commit 308580a). Add color: var(--text-black) to .toggle-btn.

openQuestions.title: Detect missing gap-decoration support live
openQuestions.detail: With the static note as the only signal, this browser shows four (two invisible) toggles that do nothing to a rule-less grid. Probe CSS.supports('row-rule-color','red') and switch the note into an explicit unsupported state while keeping the toggles driving the generated-CSS story.

openQuestions.title: Promote the repeat() alternation from comment to demo
openQuestions.detail: The full-CSS snippet shows repeat(2, 1px), 3px only as commented-out lines. A fifth toggle applying that alternating pattern would demonstrate the list/repeat grammar the feature index advertises, complementing rule-builder.

openQuestions.title: Expose toggle state and use a variable for the row-rule colour
openQuestions.detail: Add aria-pressed to the four toggles, and replace the hard-coded '#ccc' in update() with var(--bg-stone) to stay inside the design system.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/css-gap-decorations/gap-ruled-grid/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 2 pass / 6 fail / 0 blocked). Structurally one of the stronger gap-decorations concepts — real toggles, honest degrade note, correct references and an accurate before/after — but the screenshot caught a textbook invariant-6 bug: the two inactive toggle buttons are blank because the background override drops the color override. Rules do not render in this browser and the toggles were not driven headless.
